subject: Post-call: latency & streaming checklist + reproducibility protocol
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@acme-retail.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: latency & streaming checklist + reproducibility protocol

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can align the qualification run: we captured the high-level SLOs and a few streaming specifics that matter for your checkout flows.

Recap (as discussed)
- Latency target: P95 <= 120 ms for text-generation streaming (end-to-end, client-facing).
- Concurrency target: support 150–200 concurrent sessions during peak checkout bursts.
- Throughput expectation: sustained ~12 requests/sec with short spikes to 40 rps for 30–60s windows.
- Streaming behavior: server-initiated chunking (SSE/HTTP2 streams) required; must preserve ordering and support incremental tokens.

We want to make the benchmark reproducible and auditable — below are the artifacts we need from your side and the measurement definitions we'll use on our end.

Action items for Acme (please):
1) Share the prompt seeds and a representative prompt set (minimum 200 prompts; 10% edge cases). We discussed a sanitized JSONL — attaching our sample format in case helpful.
2) Confirm which endpoint semantics matter for you: strict ordering vs. best-effort (we default to strict).
3) Provide a representative QPS/arrival pattern (CSV or a short script) for the peak and baseline windows.
4) Grant read access to the evaluation harness Drive folder (link below) or provide your CI runner key so we can push the harness.

What Redwood will deliver prior to the run
- A measurement spec (definitions below), a small-run warmup checklist, and an eval harness with reproducible seed handling.
- A proposed run window — we suggest a 90-minute slot: 10m warmup, 15m baseline, 60m steady-state (with a few ramp-ups).

Measurement definitions (summary)
- First-byte latency (FBL): time from client request to first streamed token at the client.
- Per-token latency: median and tails for token emission once generation starts.
- End-to-end P50/P95/P99: measured at the client-facing gateway after all network hops.
- Throughput: successful completions/sec (excludes client disconnects).
- Concurrency: number of active KV/decoder contexts per model shard.

Attachments (stubs):
- sample-prompts.jsonl (example schema)
- redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (checklist template)

Next steps / timing
- If you can drop the prompt set and arrival CSV by EOD Tuesday (11/18), we can confirm the run and reserve capacity for Wed (11/19) or Thu (11/20).

Thanks — adding Marissa and Ben to help with the harness + infra scheduling.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

Thanks, Priyom — very helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our infra team before we hand you the prompt set: 

1) Measurement window: when you say 60m steady-state, do you sample metrics at 1s granularity or 5s? We want to ensure our agents produce the same sampling cadence.
2) KV cache / warm cache behavior: will you measure cold-starts separately? Our traffic is highly bursty and cache priming matters.
3) For streaming, do you plan to measure first-byte from an edge vantage (our CDN) or directly against the instance? We prefer edge-level so it mirrors production.

I've attached a sanitized prompt bundle (sample-prompts.jsonl) with token-length distribution and a small arrival pattern CSV. Also looping in procurement on scheduling.

Attachments: sample-prompts.jsonl (4 KB)

On timing: we can drop the full prompt set by Tue EOD as requested. For run slots, Thu morning (11/20 09:00–11:00 PT) works best for us.

Samantha Lee
Platform Lead, AI Engineering
Acme Retail

Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & streaming checklist + reproducibility protocol

Samantha — thanks for the prompt bundle and the arrival CSV. Answers below and a few additional notes.

Sampling cadence
- We'll capture internal fine-grained traces at 1s resolution and roll up to 5s buckets for public reporting. For the run report we'll publish both granular (1s) and aggregated (5s) views.

Cache/warm-starts
- We'll treat cold-starts as separate experiments. For the primary qualification run we'll start with a 10-minute controlled priming period (we'll send the warmup prompts from your seed list) then enter the steady-state. That priming will exercise KV cache and tokenizer warming.

Vantage point for streaming latency
- Agree: measuring at the CDN/edge is the right signal for you. We'll deploy a small edge probe (mirror traffic path) so reported FBL maps to what your customers see. We'll include per-hop breakdowns in the final artifact.

Reproducibility protocol (short)
- Seed handling: all prompts will be normalized (whitespace, unicode NFKC) and a deterministic RNG seed will be applied to sampling ops. Our harness will publish the seed file and the exact harness commit hash.
- Environment snapshot: kernel, runtime flags, model artifact sha, quantization profile, and GPU driver versions will be captured and included.
- Warmup recipe: 10m warmup, 5m cooldown between ramps, steady-state 60m.
- Failure handling: retry logic is out-of-band for measurement; we count retries and report both raw and retry-excluded metrics.

I've attached the eval-harness-instructions.md (stub) and the redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (template).

Proposed run window: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 09:00–10:30 PT (we'll hold 09:00–10:30 for the run and the 10:30–11:00 for a quick readout). Please confirm and we'll book infra.

Action items for Acme (updated)
- Confirm run slot by EOD Wed (11/19).
- Final prompt set + arrival CSV (you said Tue EOD; confirm).
- Provide a CDN probe endpoint (or a small read-only DNS entry) for edge vantage measurements.

Thanks — Marissa/Ben will coordinate the harness and infra reservation.

Best,
Priyom
